blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A planner adds `prob += 4000 <= lpSum(c[i] * x[i] for i in north) <= 9000, "north_band"`. The solved plan gives the north $2,500k, and the status is Optimal. What happened to the band?

options.text: CBC relaxed it, because no plan could give the north $4,000k
options.says: The status is Optimal, so CBC kept every row it received; the floor never reached it.

options.text: PuLP refused it, because a band needs a name for each side
options.says: PuLP raised nothing: the line was accepted, and only part of it became a row.

options.text: PuLP made it the objective, because it holds two comparisons
options.says: Only an expression with no comparison replaces the objective; this line gave PuLP a constraint.

options.text: Python dropped its left half, so the $4,000k floor was lost
options.says: Right: a <= b <= c is (a <= b) and (b <= c), and the and gives back its right half, so the floor is lost.

origin.section: `+=` Adds a Row Only When It Is Handed a Constraint

questions.stem: A script names a row `"cap " + region` for each region. One spreadsheet spells a region `North-East` and another `North East`, so both appear. What happens when the second of those rows is added?

options.text: PuLP raises PulpError, as both names turn into cap_North_East
options.says: Right: PuLP rewrites the space and the dash to _, so the second name repeats the first and is refused.

options.text: PuLP keeps both rows, as the two names differ as they were typed
options.says: PuLP compares names after rewriting them, and both become cap_North_East.

options.text: PuLP swaps the second row in for the first, and says nothing
options.says: A repeated row name is refused with PulpError when the second row is added; no row is replaced.

options.text: PuLP gives the second row a counter name, as its own is taken
options.says: Counter names such as _C1 go only to rows added with no name; a taken name is refused.

origin.section: Row and Variable Names Must Stay Unique After PuLP Rewrites Them

questions.stem: An old nightly job runs `if prob.solve(PULP_CBC_CMD(msg=0)): send(read_plan(x))`, where `read_plan` lists the variables above 0.5. Tonight the must-do projects cost more than the budget. What does the job do?

options.text: It sends nothing, since the solve returns a false value
options.says: The solve returns -1 for Infeasible, and Python treats every number but 0 as true.

options.text: It sends a plan built from leftover values, since -1 is true
options.says: Right: the branch runs on -1, and the variables still hold what CBC had when it gave up.

options.text: It stops on an error, since no variable has a value to read
options.says: After an infeasible run the variables still hold numbers, one binary even at -0.469; nothing raises.

options.text: It sends last night's plan, since tonight's solve kept no values
options.says: Tonight's run overwrote the values with its own leftovers; nothing of last night's plan is read.

origin.section: Read `status` and `sol_status` Before Any Value, and Expect None
